report:
Reviewed the full body_independence claim, all eight ordinary implementation associations and the sole associated TODO test. The obligations are that a checked signature supplies types, binder and parameter environment as the cross-item interface; obtaining it does not check the definition body or read body semantics; and signature lowering does not invoke any function body query. Captured checking.sage and the linked architectural-foundations RFD. Its cross-item-dependency section explicitly distinguishes semantic dependency from provisional coarse inputs: a coarse input may cause signature reexecution, while equal interface values must backdate before downstream consumers. Thus opening a CST containing a body field is not itself evidence that the signature checks that body or semantically consumes its expression tree.

Implementation inspection: LocalFnSym::sig in fns.rs opens the source but accesses owner information, declared generics, parameter/receiver types, return type and where clauses. It never traverses cst.body or invokes body(). open_owner obtains a trait/impl signature, copying its existing generics, Self type and predicates. The resulting FnSig contains the parameter and return types, owner receiver facts and CheckedParameterEnv under its binder. LocalFnSym::body is a separate query which consumes sig; there is no reverse signature-to-body edge. Impl sig lowers its generics, self type, trait reference and header predicates; trait sig lowers explicit generics, implicit Self and predicates and marks unsupported header features, without checking member bodies. CheckGenerics in cst/generics.rs only mints/binds declaration parameters. TypeCst::check in cst/ty.rs recursively checks type syntax and type arguments, resolves identities, retains alias applications, and imports external nominal declaration environments; no expression body checker is called. trait_env::lower_predicates traverses declared generic bounds and where clauses and asks trait signatures for eligibility. Check::complete_parameter_env in sig.rs combines declared and type-use predicates with eligibility, and finish returns an owned checked value, without body computation.

external_fn_signature in external_syms.rs asks TcxDb for keyed raw function signature metadata and lower_fn_signature builds types, binder, owner facts, receiver and predicates in Sage storage. Its lower_generics/lower_predicate/lower_ty helpers lower owned metadata and carry unsupported completeness explicitly; they do not query Sage bodies. Captured TcxDb function signature interface documents the metadata product; captured FnSymbol and TraitSymbol dispatch confirms the local/external signature routes. Captured cst/paths.rs and resolver source show the type-path dependency resolves ribs/module identities and recursively checks type arguments, rather than checking function bodies. This assessment concerns the represented interface boundaries, not an assertion that every future Rust signature feature is implemented.

The associated test todo::checking_signature_body_independence contains no assertions. Its explicit TODO calls for local and external caller query traces naming selected interface facts and excluding bodies, plus a body-only edit that preserves the signature result and avoids consumer reexecution. This is accepted deferred verification, not an ordinary passing test or established full conformance matrix. Completing it requires source-backed callers and callees, query observation distinguishing signature and body operations, and a persistent database edit sequence comparing interface results and downstream execution. Those tests must account for the RFD's coarse-input allowance rather than demanding that a signature can never reexecute. The comment already captures the outstanding cross-item and incremental cases; no additional requested source edits were identified.

Commands executed: fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions, source inspection, and review read captures of design/RFD, type-path/resolver helpers, symbol signature dispatch and metadata interface. No tests or build were executed by this reviewer; centrally reported suite success is separate from this source assessment. No source changes. The review records implementation inspection with the existing test TODO visibly retained.
